description: Tree, 10–40 m high, 60–250 cm girth. Lateral buds ellipsoid, ca 1 mm long, glabrous. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, blackish or dark brown when dry. Bark greyish-brown to dark brown, densely lenticellate, flaky and longitudinally fissured; inner bark granular, reddish, brownish or yellow; sapwood yellowish-white. Stipules triangular, 1.5 by 1 mm. Leaves elliptic oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 5.5–13 by 1.5–4 cm; base obtuse to slightly oblique; apex caudate, acuminate or cuspidate; margins serrate in the upper half; subcoriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and pale on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface and subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–11 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces, scalariform and reticulate veins hardly distinct on either surface. Petiole 1–1.4 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences: male and female separate, rarely mixed, erect, terminal or axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence much branched or simple, spikelets 8–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish, solitary, rarely in clusters; bracts and bracteoles triangular, 1.5–2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, ovate or obovate 1.5–2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 10–12, glabrous, 2–3 mm long; rudimentary ovary globose, ca 0.5 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescences spike 8–15 cm long. Female flowers as male; styles 3, divergent, stigmata blunt, glabrous. Fruits sessile, globose or ovoid, 1–1.5 by 0.8–1.3 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence 9–12 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing but not fused with the nut; wall sparsely covered with simple spines, curved beyond their bases, pubescent then glabrescent; dehiscent. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, ca 1 cm in diam., glabrous.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis acuminatissima. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 185. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 12–30 m high, 60–200 cm girth. Lateral buds ovoid 3–4 by 2–3 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, blackish, lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, roughly scaly, longitudinally furrowed; inner bark with dense, irregular, narrow, pale brown ridges. Stipules lanceolate, 3–5 by 1–1.5 mm, ciliate, pubescent outside. Leaves elliptic, broadly elliptic, elliptic or oblong, 10–20 by 4–7 cm; base obtuse, oblique or slightly cuneate; apex blunt or acute, rarely acuminate or cuspidate; margins entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface, pubescent on the lower; midrib prominent on both surfaces; lateral nerves 7–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface, reticulate veins conspicuous on the upper. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, pubescent, glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, axillary or terminal, pubescent to tomentose. Male inflorescence much branched, spikelets 7–12 cm long. Male flowers greenish or whitish, smell disagreeable, in 3–7-flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles round to acute, 1.5–3 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes ovate, acute, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 2.2–3.2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, 1–2 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence single or branched spikes, spikelets 5–20 cm long. Female flowers as male; styles 1.5–2 mm long, hairy in lower half, divergent, stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, globose, 4–6 cm in diam. (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence 15–30 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing but not fused with the nut; wall densely covered with branched spines, almost obscuring, branches of spines erect and hairy; indehiscent. Nuts 1–(3) per cupule, ovoid, 2–2.5 by 1–1.5 cm, tomentose throughout; scar ca 0.5 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis argentea. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 187. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 9–20 m high, 60–200 cm girth. Lateral buds ovoid, with acuminate scales. Twigs densely pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark blackish, lenticellate, deeply furrowed. Leaves obovate, elliptic, to oblong, 12–17 by 4–7.5 cm; base cuneate; apex acute, obtuse or acuminate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and light tan on the lower; midrib prominent on both surfaces; lateral nerves 6–10 pairs, sharply ridged, prominent and arched but not anastomosing on the lower surface and slightly depressed on the upper, scalariform and reticulate veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–1.7 cm long; glabrous, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, axillary or terminal. Male inflorescence with few to many branches spikelets 5–12 cm long, hairy throughout. Male flowers white, fragrant, in 1–3-5-flowered cluster; calyx 6, free, lobes 1–2 by 0.5 mm, incurved stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose ca 0.5 mm in diam., glabrous. Female inflorescence spike to 25 cm long. Female flowers in 1–5 flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles hairy; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, globose or ovoid, ca 4 cm in diam. (including cupule), on erect infructescence 10–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall with simple and branched woody spines, the latter erect and pubescent near base. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, conical 1–1.5 cm in diam., at both ends more or less oblique; scar flattened, ca 1 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Tree, 8–20 m high, 80–180 cm girth. Terminal buds and lateral ellipsoid or ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm; bracts ca 2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs pubescent then glabrous, lenticellate. Bark dark green or brown, roughly, vertically cracked, irregularly fissured; sapwood white. Leaves elliptic, oblong or obovate-oblong, 10–23 by 3.5–10 cm; base acute to broadly obtuse; apex acute, acuminate to obtuse; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous, dark glossy green on the upper surface and pale on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper, scalariform veins dominant on the lower surface, reticulate veins indistinct. Petiole 1.5–2 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescences always branched, spikelets 3–9 cm long; bracts and bracteoles triangular, ca 1 by 1.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white to yellowish, scented, solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, obovate, 1.5–2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 6–(12); rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 10–15 cm long. Female flowers solitary, rarely in clusters, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, stigmata pointed. Fruits ovoid, 5–6 cm in diam. (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence 10–25 cm long, always clustering by erect spines in groups of 2–3 on the rachis. Cupule completely enclosed except the umbo, and partly fused with the nut; wall completely covered by the tufted, erect, simple spines. Nuts solitary, ovoid, 1.5–2.5 by 1–2 cm; scar more than half the length of the nut and fused with the inner side of the cupule.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Tree, 10–18 m high, 80–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 mm in diam.; bracts pubescent outside. Twigs tomentose, then glabrescent, lenticellate. Stipules ovate, ca 2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Leaves oblong, 10–16 by 4.5–5 cm; base obtuse, slightly oblique, apex obtuse, blunt, acute or shortly acuminatel; margins entire; subcoriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and dull, pale on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface and subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–15, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface and hardly distinct on the upper; reticulate veins slightly distinct on the upper surface. Petiole 1.5–2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences males and females separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence a branched panicle, 3–5 cm long; bracts and bracteoles triangular, 4–5 by 2 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6 lobed, lobes triangular, ca 2 by 1 mm, hairy outside; stamens 10–12, 1.5–2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam. Female inflorescence spike 8–15 cm long. Female flowers always solitary, not in clusters, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, ovoid, ca 3 cm in diam.(including cupule), solitary or 2–3-clustered held by their spines, on erect infructescence, 8–20 cm long. Cupule enclosing up to ¾ of the nut; wall completely covered by the tufted, erect, simple spines. Nuts (2)–3 per cupule, ca 1 by 1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Tree, 6–20 m high, 100–200 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, hairy outside. Twigs stout, quadrangular, pubescent then glabrescent, sparsely lenticellate. Bark brown, fissured. Leaves obovate or oblanceolate, 14–20 by 5–9 cm; base cuneate; apex obtuse or broadly acute; margins serrate; coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and pale on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 14–22 pairs, straight and reaching the points of serrate margins, scalariform veins conspicious on the lower surface. Petiole slender, 1–3 cm long, eglandular, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed. Male inflorescence always branched, terminal or axillary, spikelets 4–10 cm long. Male flowers white or whitish-yellow, in 2–5 flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate, free, ca 1.5 by 0.5 mm, glabrous; stamens 12, 1.5–2 mm long; bracts ovate, ca 2 by 1.5 mm glabrous; rudimentary ovary 3-lobed, villous. Female inflorescence spike, axillary, up to 8 cm long. Female flowers not clustered, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3(4) ca 1 mm long; stigmata divergent, all glabrous. Fruits sessile, ovoid, 1–1.6 by 1–1.2 cm, (including cupule), on erect infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule enclosing up to ½ of the nut; wall with thin imbricate scales or lamella, the latter acute, free and erect at apex. Nut 1, ovoid, rarely flattened, 1–1.5 by 0.9–1.5 cm, glabrous except around the umbo.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Tree, 10–20 m high, 40–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 4–5 by 2–3 mm. Twigs at first ferruginous, then glabrescent, tetra-to pentangulate, lenticellate. Bark grey, shallowly fissured; inner bark ca 2 cm thick, yellow with white stripes. Stipules narrowly lanceolate, 4 5 by 1.5–2 mm, glabrous. Leaves oblanceolate, 13–29 by 4–11 cm; base cuneate; apex acute, broadly acute to obtuse; margins serrate; coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and greenish to glaucous on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface and slightly depressed on the upper, pubescent then glabrescent; lateral nerves 14–17 pairs, narrowly ridged on the lower surface and subdepressed on the upper, glabrous, scalariform veins conspicuous on both surfaces. Petiole 1.5–2.3 cm long, flattened adaxially, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed. Male inflorescence always branched, terminal or axillary, spikelets 7–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish-cream, scented, in 1–8–10 flowered cluster; bracts ovate, glabrous; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, glabrous; stamens (10)–12, 1–1.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ca 1 mm in diam. Female inflorescence spike, axillary, 8–12 cm long, pubescent, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3; stigmata erect to divergent. Fruits obconical, 1.5–3.2 by 1–3 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence 15–20 cm long, fruit-stalk 0.5–1 cm. Cupule enclosing up to ¾ of the nut (when young completely enclosed except around the umbo); wall with thin imbricate scales or lamellae, the latter truncate and fused with the wall or curved inwards. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, conical 1.5–2.3 by 1–1.8 cm, glossy brown; scar flattened, ca 8 mm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis cerebrina. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 197. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 6–20 m high; 40–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 3–5 by 2–3 mm, scales ovate, acute, 3–4 by 2–3 mm. Twigs densely tomentose, then glabrescent, sparsely lenticellate. Bark smooth, shedding profusely; inner bark fibrous, yellowish; sapwood pale yellow. Stipules linear-triangular, ca 13 by 1.2 mm. Leaves oblong, 12–24 by 4–9.5 cm; base obtuse, slightly acute, sometimes unequal; apex cuspidate or caudate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous except along midrib on the upper surface, pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface and faint on the upper; lateral nerves 14–19 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins finely conspicuous on the lower surface and hardly distinct on the upper, reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, pubescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 4–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, 1–1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, 1.5–0.5 mm, tomentose outside; stamens 12, 2.2–3.3 mm long; rudimentary ovary globose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 15–20 cm long, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, 1–1.5 mm long; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile or up to 0.5 cm pedicellate, ovoid and depressed on top, 1–1.5 by 1.5–3 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence, 10–25 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except around umbo, but not fused to nut; wall sparsely covered with simple, curled to adaxial spines, pubescent then glabrescent; rarely dehiscent. Nuts 1–(3) per cupule, ovoid and depressed on both sides, ca 1 by 1.5 cm, adpressed with silky hairs.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis costata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 199. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 5–20 m high, 50–150 cm girth. Twigs glabrous, lenticellate. Bark greenish-brown, ca 2 cm thick, fissured. Leaves lanceolate rarely ovate, 9–16 by 2–6 cm; base acute, obtuse, usually equal; apex acuminate or caudate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, dark glossy green on the upper surface and pale on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 6–9 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, conspicuous on both surfaces, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface and reticulate veins conspicuous on the upper. Petiole 0.8–1.5 cm, glabrous, black when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence with few branches, spikelets 4–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate ca 1.5 by 0.3 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate, ca 2 by 1 mm, glabrous except ciliate margins; stamens 12, ca 3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ovoid or conical, ca 0.5 mm in diam., pubescent. Female inflorescence spike 10–20 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile or up to 2 mm long pedicellate, ovoid or obovoid, 2–2.5 cm in diam. (including cupule), often in clusters of 2–3-fruits at intervals with solitary fruits on erect influctescence 10–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines (when young with a narrow spineless line from top to base adaxially). Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid or obovoid 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 cm, usually asymmetrical, covered by grey indumentum, then glossy brown except umbo; scar basal; ca 0.5 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis crassifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 199. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 10–30 m high; 150–200 cm girth. Terminal buds and lateral ovoid; bracts 2–3 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent on both sides. Twigs tomentose, then glabrescent. Bark brown with grey patches; inner bark with long, pale stripes. Leaves elliptic or oblong, 11–22 by 5–10 cm; base obtuse, sometimes slightly oblique; apex acuminate; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous except along midrib and nerves on the upper surface, pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–14 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface; reticulate veins inconspicuous. Petiole 1–1.5 cm long, tomentose then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female mixed or separate, terminal and axillary, erect, tomentose. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 5–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 4–5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers creamy, fragrant, solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, oblong, free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, ciliate; stamens 12, 1.5–2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ovoid, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 8–15 cm long. Female flowers always solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, pilose near base; stigmata pointed, more or less hairy. Fruits globose, 4–6.5 cm in diam. (including cupule), always solitary on erect and woody infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines. Nuts 1 (2–3) per cupule, ovoid to ellipsoid, 1–1.5 cm in diam.; glabrous except orbicular area of indumentum around umbo; scar basal.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis diversifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 201. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 10–30 m high; 50–150 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticels scattered; inner bark dark brown; sapwood white with brownish stripes at intervals. Leaves lanceolate, lanceolate-oblong or elliptic, 12–21 by 3–5.5 cm; base slightly cuneate, obtuse or oblique; apex acuminate or caudate; margins entire; subcoriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, glossy green on the upper surface and greyish-brown on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves sharply ridged on the lower surface and more or less depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 10–18 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface and subdepressed on the upper; reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, pubescent then glabrous, black when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, axillary and terminal, pubescent. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 4–12 cm long; bracts and bracteoles triangular, ca 2 by 2 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate, free, ca.1 by 0.4 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, ca 1.5 mm long, glabrous, rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 0.5 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 15–20 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, ovoid, 2–3 cm in diam. (including cupule), often in 2–3-flowered cluster fruits, interspersed with solitary ones, on erect infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines (irregular, diffuse and sparse throughout when young). Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, 1.3–1.5 by 0.9–1 cm, usually asymmetrical, covered by grey indumentum then glossy green, except the umbo; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis ferox. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 205. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 15–20 m high; 90–120 cm girth. Twigs with reddish hairs, glabrescent, lenticellate. Inner bark yellowish-red; sapwood whitish-brown. Leaves obovate or obovate-elliptic, 18–25 by 6–9.5 cm; base slightly narrowed to the base; apex broadly acute or acute; margins serrate; coriaceous, glossy green on the upper surface, pale and tawny pubescent on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface and flattened on the upper; lateral nerves 14–17 pairs, straight and reaching the points of the serrate margins, scalariform and reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, usually with an adaxial gland. Inflorescences male and female usually mixed, sometimes separate. Male inflorescence always branched, terminal or axillary, spikelets 10–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish-white or yellow, in 1–3-flowered cluster; bracts broadly triangular, glabrous; calyx (5–) 6-lobed, lobes free, ca 1.5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 10, ca 2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ovoid, ca 1 mm in diam., hairy. Female inflorescence spike, solitary, rarely branched, 5–10 cm long, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3(4) divergent. Fruits ovoid, 2–2.5 by 1.5–2 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence 7–10 cm long; fruit stalk 2–3 mm long. Cupule enclosing up to ½ of the nut (when young completely enclosed); wall with thin imbricate scales or lamellae, lamellae acute, free and erect at apex. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, ca 2 by 1.7 cm, glossy brown, with indumentum around the umbo.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis fissa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 207. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 10–15 m high; 30–40 cm girth. Axillary buds globose, ca 2 by 2 mm; bracts hirsute outside, reddish brown hairy inside. Leaves oblong or oblong-lanceolate, usually curved to one side, 12–18 by 5–6.5 cm; base oblique, broadly acute to minutely cordate; apex acuminate or acute; margins entire; coriaceous, softly woolly on the lower surface, greyish-green and glabrous except along midrib and nerves on the upper; midrib and lateral nerves prominent beneath and depressed on the upper surface; lateral nerves 13–17 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface and slightly depressed on the upper. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, densely tomentose. Male inflorescence not seen. Female inflorescence spike 3–7 cm long, axillary and near terminal, densely greenish-grey hairy; bracts and bracteoles ovate, 1–3 by 1–1.5 mm, hairy outside, glabrous inside, ciliate. Female flowers simple, pubescent; ovary ovoid, 1–1.5 mm in diam., hirsute; styles 3, erect to divergent, hairy in lower half; stigmata pointed, glabrous. Fruits globose, ca 2 by 2 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence, 3–7 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall with branched and silky spines. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, conical apex, ca 1 by 1 cm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis fordii. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 207. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 7–30 m high, 50–250 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–6 by 3–4 mm; bracts pubescent outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark brownish or greyish, thick scaly; inner bark yellowish; sapwood white. Leaves oblong, ovate or slightly obovate, 10–20 by 4–10 cm; base obtuse, equal or suboblique; apex acute, acuminate, sometimes obtuse; margins serrate in upper half to two-thirds; coriaceous, glabrous except along midrib above, densely pubescent below; midrib and nerves prominent below, more or less depressed above; lateral nerves 15–21 pairs, rather straight to the end of the serrate margins, scalariform veins fine but distinct below. Petiole 1.5–2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, tomentose. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 10–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles triangular, ca 1.5 by 1.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white, scented, solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate, free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 6–12, ca 2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 8–25 cm long. Female flowers always solitary, not in clusters, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, pilose at base; stigmata pointed, blackish. Fruits sessile, ovoid, 1.5–4 cm in diam. (including cupule), clustering by their spines in groups of 2–3 alternating with solitary fruit on an erect infructescence 15–30 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines. Nut 1 per cupule, conical or ovoid, 1.3–1.5 by 0.8–1.1 cm, usually curved to one side; scar ca 1 cm in diam.; at base or rather above.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Castanopsis indica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 9. Part 3, 2008. Pg. 211. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, 9–20 m high, 40–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid-ellipsoid, ca 3 by 5 mm, scales ovate, acute, ca 5 by 2 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs pubescent then glabrous, sparsely lenticellate, blackish when dry. Bark ca 2 cm thick, grey, shallowly reticulate fissured; inner bark dirty brown or whitish; sapwood white; heartwood brown. Stipules triangular, ca 1 mm, caducous. Leaves obovate, obovate-oblong, oblong or lanceolate, 7–17 by 5–7 cm; base slightly cuneate, obtuse; apex acute or obtuse; margins entire or sometimes serrate; subcoriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface and pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface and depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 7–12 pairs, distinct on the lower surface and slightly depressed on the upper, scalariform and reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female mixed or separate, terminal or axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 10–15 cm; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 0.5 by 0.5 mm, tomentose outside. Male flowers white to yellowish, scented, usually in 3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, obovate, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, glabrous, stamens 12, 2–3 mm long; rudimentary ovary ovoid, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence always spike 10–15 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3–5-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, hairy near base; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, irregularly globose, 1.5–2.5 by 1.5–3.5 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo and more or less fused with nut; wall sparsely covered with simple, short, curled spines set in 3–5 lines. Nuts (1)–2–3 per cupule, ovoid, ca 1 by 1 cm, usually emarginate at apex.

description: Tree, 15–20 m high; 150–200 cm girth. Terminal buds globose, ca 3 by 3 mm; bracts ovate, acute, pubescent outside, ciliate. Twigs with reddish-brown indumentum, then glabrescent. Bark dark brown, fissured. Stipules lanceolate, 3–4 by 1.5 mm, hairy. Leaves elliptic, obovate or oblong, 8–17 by 4–6 cm; base slightly cuneate, usually asymmetrical; apex shortly cuspidate, blunt, acute or acuminate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface and pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; lateral nerves 8–10 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower. Petiole 0.8–1.2 cm, pubescent then glabresceent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 10–20 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white, solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes oblong or spathulate, free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, 2.5–3 mm, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, 1–1.5 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 10–15 cm long. Female flowers always solitary not in clusters, other characters as in male flowers, styles 3, divergent, pubescent; stigmata pointed, glabrous. Fruits ovoid, depressed on top, 3–4 cm in diam. (including cupule), solitary on erect and woody infructescence 10–25 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo but not fused, inside densely silky hairy; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines; dehiscent. Nut 1 per cupule, rounded and depressed on both sides, 1.5–1.8 by 2–2.5 cm densely brown hairy; scar basal; up to 2 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 14–20 m high, 80–150 cm girth. Axillary buds curved, tubular, ca 0.5 cm long. Twigs glabrous, lenticellate. Bark greyish-black, inner bark ca 1 cm thick, yellow with brown stripes. Leaves lanceolate or oblong, 10–15 by 3.5–5 cm; base slightly cuneate; obtuse or oblique; apex acuminate, caudate or acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous, glabrous on the upper surface, sparsely pubescent then glabrous on the lower; midrib prominent on both surfaces; lateral nerves 12–15 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, slightly prominent on both surfaces, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female always separate. Male inflorescence terminal, branched, spikelets 3–8 cm long, densely ferruginous. Male flowers yellow, scented, in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6, ca 1 mm long, united in lower half, lobes triangular, pubescent outside; stamens 12, glabrous, 6 longer and 6 shorter the longer ca 3 mm, the shorter 1–1.5 mm; rudimentary ovary a square column, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, glabrous. Female inflorescence spike to 20 cm long, axillary and terminal, flowers solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent. Fruits ovoid or obovoid, ca 2 by 1 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence, 10–15 cm long, fruit sessile or with stalk to 1 mm. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall with thin imbricate scales or lamellae when young , 4–5 undulate lines when mature. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, apex conical, ca 1 by 0.5 cm (young), mature ca 2.5 by 2 cm.

description: Tree, 10–15 m high, 60–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 2–3 by 1–2 mm, scales ovate, acute, tomentose outside. Bark yellowish-brown, longitudinally furrowed. Leaves ovate or oblong, 8–15 by 3–5 cm; base obtuse, oblique; apex acuminate to bluntly acuminate; margins entire; subcoriaceous or coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, reddish-brown on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–10 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 0.8–1 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, erect, rufous. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 4–7 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers in 3-flowered cluster, calyx 6-lobed, oblong, free, ca 1.5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 3.2–4.3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, 1.5–2 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence not seen. Fruits ovoid, free, 5–6 by 4–5 cm (including cupule), always solitary on erect and woody infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple, dehiscent spines. Nut 1 per cupule, ellipsoid, 3–3.5 by 2 cm, flattened to one longitudinal side, glabrous except for a star-shaped area of indumentum around the umbo; scar basal, small.

description: Tree, 15–20 m high; buttress to 2 m. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 5 by 3 mm, with reddish brown indumentum. Twigs glabrous with sparse leaf scars and lenticels. Bark flaky or smooth, yellowish grey. Stipules linear, ca 5 by 2 mm long, with reddish-brown indumentum outside. Leaves oblong, 7.5–22 by 2.5–11 cm; base obtuse, minutely oblique; apex acuminate, obtuse; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, pubescent along nerves on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 11–16 pairs, rather straight then arched near margins, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1.5–3 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, axillary or terminal, pubescent. Male inflorescence much branched, spikelets 4–8 cm long. Male flowers in 1–3-flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles triangular, with reddish-brown indumentum outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes oblong, ca 7 mm long, hairy outside; stamens 12, glabrous, ca 2 mm long; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 10–15 cm long. Female flowers as male; styles 3, divergent, hairy near base; stigmata pointed. Fruits globose or ovoid, 5–9 by 4–7 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence 15–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing and fused with the nut; wall densely covered with branched, pointed spines, until it is hardly visible, spines pubescent then glabrescent, dehiscent. Nuts 1–4 per cupule, ovoid or ellipsoid, usually flattened on one longitudinal side, 4–5 by 2.5–3 cm, hairy throughout, scar 0.5–1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 10–15 m high, 60–90 cm girth. Twigs sparsely pubescent, then glabrous, rounded lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, roughly grooved; inner bark with yellow and purple stripes. Leaves elliptic or oblong, 10–17 by 3–6.5 cm; base obtuse, suboblique; apex acuminate or cuspidate to caudate; margins entire or serrate in the upper half; subcoriaceous or coriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, usually purple when dry; lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, ridged on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, terminal or axillary. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 5–10 cm long. Male flowers solitary, yellowish or white; bracts and bracteoles ca 1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes nearly free, ca 1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, ca 4 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, 0.5 mm in diam., hairy. Female inflorescence spike or 2–3 branched, spikelets 8–15 cm long, pubescent, solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits obovoid, always asymmetric, usually flattened adaxially, 2.5–3 by 2–2.5 cm (including cupule), fruit stalk 2–3 mm long, on erect woody infructescence 8–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing and fused with the nut; wall sparsely with short woody spines, 2–3 branched reclining and decurved; indehiscent. Nuts 1 per cupule, ovoid, usually depressed to one longitudinal side, 2–2.2 by 1.5–1.7 cm.

description: Tree, 7–25 m high, 70–180 cm girth. Axillary buds ovoid, laterally compressed. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, rather smooth; inner bark reddish brown with white stripes. Leaves lanceolate or oblong, 10–20 by 3–6 cm; base cuneate, obtuse to oblique; apex acute, acuminate to cuspidate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous, dull green on the upper surface, pale or glaucous on the lower; midrib prominent on both surfaces; lateral nerves 7–11 pairs, distinct on the lower surfaces, subdepressed on the upper, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2 cm, glabrous, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female mixed or separate, erect, axillary or terminal, spike or rarely branched. Male inflorescence a spike or with spikelets 6–15 cm long, pubescent. Male flowers yellow, scented, 1–3-flowered in a bract; bracts and bracteoles ovate, pubescent outside; calyx 6-lobed, ovate or obovate, ca 2 by 1 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 3–3.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 15–20 cm long. Female flower solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, globose or bilobed, 4–6 cm in diam. (including cupule) on erect woody infructescence 15–30 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut but not fused with it, sparsely hairy inside; wall sparsely covered with woody, branched, curved spines; dehiscent. Nuts 1–3–(4) per cupule, ovoid in outline, sometimes curved to one side, densely white hairy around the umbo.

description: Tree, 6–30 m high. Bark greenish-brown or greenish-grey; inner bark brown or pinkish. Leaves elliptic or oblong, 8–16 by 3–6 cm; base slightly cuneate acute; apex acuminate or acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous, glabrous glossy green on the upper surface, pale brown on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–11 pairs, conspicuous on both sides, scalariform and reticulate veins distinct on both sides when dry. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female usually separate. Male inflorescence much branched, axillary or terminal, spikelets 8–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish, in clusters of 3 or more; bracts pilose outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, ca 2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ovoid, ca 0.5 mm in diam., erect, hairy. Female inflorescence spike solitary, 8–10 cm long. Female flowers in clusters of 1–3, bracts and calyx as in male; staminodes 12; styles 3, divergent, glabrous. Fruits turbinate or pyriform, 2.5–3 by 2–3 cm (including cupule) on erect infructescence 10–15 cm long, fruit stalk 0.5–1 cm. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall smooth, without scales or spines, with 3–4 conspicuous, undulate lines outside. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, 2–2.3 by 2.3–2.7 cm, silky hairy around the umbo.

description: Tree, 5–20 m high, 70–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–6 by 2–3 mm; bracts hairy outside. Twigs dark brown tomentose then glabrescent, with sparse, round lenticels. Bark brown to dark brown, longitudinally furrowed; inner bark reddish-brown with pale longitudinal stripes. Leaves ovate or obovate, 6–10 by 3–7 cm; base obtuse to slightly cuneate; apex acute or obtuse to shortly acuminate, usually with minute emarginate tip; margins slightly serrate in the upper half to entire and revolute; coriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface; midrib and lateral nerves raised sharply on the lower; lateral nerves 5–7 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 4–5 mm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, terminal or axillary. Male inflorescences much branched, spikelets 4–7 cm long, pubescent. Male flowers whitish to yellowish, solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles ovate, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, hairy outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate or spathulate, free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 11–12, 2–2.5 mm long, pubescent outside, ciliate; rudimentary ovary globose, ca 1 mm in diam., hairy. Female inflorecence spike to few branched, spikelets 8–17 cm long, pubescent. Female flowers as male; styles 3, hairy in lower half; stigmata pointed. Fruits ovoid, 1–2.5 cm in diam. (including cupule), sessile, on erect infructescence, 8–17 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall sparsely covered with woody, branched, decurved spines set in 4–5 irregular lines; indehiscent. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid to ellipsoid, 1.3–1.5 by 1–1.2 cm, more or less glossy brown; scar flattened, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 6–25 m high, 60–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 4–5 by 3 mm, sparsely pubescent. Twigs pubescent to glabrescent, with round lenticels. Bark deeply furrowed, brown to greyish-brown, defoliating in small flakes; inner bark yellowish to pinkish-brown, with white stripes. Leaves oblong, elliptic or obovate, 10–25 by 3.2–6.3 cm; base slightly acute or obtuse, asymmetrical; apex acute, acuminate, sometimes obtuse;margins entire; subcoriaceous, glabrous and glossy dark green on the upper surface, sparsely pubescent on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–11 pairs, conspicuous on the upper surface, scalariform veins distinct on both sides. Petiole 1.5–4 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, terminal or axillary. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 8–15 cm long, pubescent. Male flowers yellow, scented; bracts and bracteoles ca 1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside, always in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes spathulate or oblong, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, glabrous; stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam.; hirsute. Female inflorescence spike or 1–2 branched, spikelet 5–15 cm long, pubescent, solitary or in (1)–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits globose, 4.5–6 cm in diam. (including cupule), fruit stalk 2–5 mm long, on erect woody infructescence 10–25 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut but not fused with it, inner part with adpressed, white, silky hairs, wall sparsely covered with woody, branched, curved spines; dehiscent. Nuts 1–3(4) per cupule, ovoid and compressed along one longitudinal side, 2–3 by 1 cm, sparsely, adpressed white hairy.

description: Tree, 10–15 m high, 50–80 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent. Leaves oblong, elliptic or obovate, 10–20 by 3.5–8 cm; base slightly cuneate, usually unequal; apex acute or obtuse, usually folded to one side; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, except along midrib; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform and reticulate veins conspicuous on the lower. Petiole 1–1.5 cm long, glabrous, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 5–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 1.5 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 2–3–5-flowered cluster; calyx 6 lobed, lobes united near base, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, ca 3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 8–15 cm long. Female flowers almost always solitary, rarely in 2–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits sessile, ovoid, 3–4 cm in diam. (including cupule), always solitary on erect infructescence, 12–20 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines. Nut 1 per cupule, globose or conical, 1.8–2 by 1.5–1.8 cm, slightly flattened at adaxial side; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 10–25 m high, 80–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 5 by 3 mm; bracts ovate, pubescent outside. Twigs slightly 4-angled, densely tomentose then glabresent. Stipules narrowly lanceolate, 5–10 by 1–2 mm, hairy on both sides. Leaves oblong, obovate oblong or elliptic, 13–28 by 5–11.5 cm; base slightly cuneate, obtuse; apex cuspidate or acute; margins entire; coriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent except along midrib and nerves on the upper surface and densely pubescent on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, terminal and axillary, villous. Male inflorescence branched, spikelets 3–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 2 by 1 mm, hairy outside, ciliate. Male flowers solitary or in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes obovate, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, ca 2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, flattened on top, hirsute. Female inflorescence spike or few branched, spikelets 15–25 cm long. Female flowers usually 3-flowered in a cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits globose, 5–6 cm in diam. (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence, 15–25 cm long, always clustering by erect spines. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo, and fused with part of it; wall completely covered by tufted, erect, simple spines. Nut (1)2–4 per cupule, ovoid, ca 2 by 0.6 cm, strongly depressed on one or two sides; scar only at base of nut, fused with cupule only at base.

description: Tree, 5–25 m high, 100–120 cm girth, usually with buttresses to 1 m high. Terminal buds ovoid to elliptic, 3–5 by 2–3 mm, scales ovate, pubescent outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrous, sparsely lenticellate. Bark smooth, grey. Stipules linear, 3–7 mm long, caducous. Leaves ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate-oblong, 9–19 by 2.5–7 cm; base obtuse to acute; apex acuminate, cuspidate or blunt acute; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glossy dark green on the upper surface, pale on the lower, pubescent then glabrous; midrib prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface, reticulate veins fine, conspicuous on the upper. Petiole 1.5–3 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed, erect, terminal or axillary. Male inflorescence always branched, spikelets 8–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish, in 3–7-flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles ovate, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, hairy outside; calyx 6-lobed, lobes oblong, free, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary globose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike to few branched, spikelets 6–10 cm long, pubescent as male flowers; styles 3, 1–1.5 mm long, divergent; stigmata pointed. Fruits obovoid, sometimes distinctly 4-lobed, 3–5 cm in diam. (including cupule), fruit stalk ca 1 cm long, on erect and robust infructescence, 4–7 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing and fused with the nut; wall with branched and simple woody spines, spines always curved and glabrous; dehiscent in (3)–4 parts when dry. Nuts 2–3, rarely one per cupule, ovoid, apex conical, ca 1.5 by 1.5 cm; scar flattened, ca 1 cm in diam.
creator: Rachun Pooma

description: Tree, to 20 m high. Twigs ferruginous when young, then glabrescent, angulate and lenticellate. Leaves oblong or obovate-oblong, rarely elliptic, 11–20 by 4.5–8 cm; base cuneate; apex acute; margins serrate; coriaceous, glabrous on the upper surface, tomentose then glabrescent on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, slightly depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 16–18 pairs, narrowly ridged on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper, scalariform veins conspicuous on both surfaces. Petiole 1–2 cm long, flattened adaxially, glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or mixed. Male inflorescences always branched, terminal or axillary, spikelets 7–15 cm long. Male flowers yellowish-cream, scented, in 1–8–10-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes free, ca 1 by 0.5 mm, glabrous; bracts ovate, glabrous; stamens (10)–12, 1–1.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary ca 1 mm in diam. Female inflorescence spike, axillary, 8–12 cm long, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3; stigmata straight to divergent. Fruits subglobose or obconical, 1.5–3.2 by 1.3 cm (including cupule), on erect infructescence 15–20 cm long, fruit-stalk 0.5–1 cm. Cupule enclosing up to three-quarters of the nut (when young completely enclosed except around the umbo); wall with thin, imbricate and tomentose scales or lamellae; more or less conspicuously 5–6 ringed when mature with truncate apex. Nut 1 per cupule, ovoid, conical, ca 1.2 by 1 cm, glossy brown; scar upcurved, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, to 20 m high. Lateral buds flattened, 0.4–0.5 by 0.2 mm, scales hooked; terminal buds ovoid, 9–10 by 3–4 mm, scales imbricate, with adpressed silver hairs along the midline and near the apex outside. Leaves oblong or oblong-ellipic, 10–12 by 3–4 cm; base cuneate to obtuse, more or less equal sided; apex cuspidate, caudate or bluntly acute; margins serrate on ⅓ to the apex; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous except along midrib near base on the upper surface and densely short pubescent especially along nerves on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface, more or less depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 12–15 pairs, rigid and curved near margins, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, densely blackish-grey hairy. Male inflorescence not seen. Female inflorescence spike or branched, spikelets terminal or axillary, 3–5 cm long, densely grey pubescent; bracts ca 10 by 3 mm, silver hairy outside. Male flowers solitary or in 1–2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, lobes ovate, sparsely hairy outside, ciliate; staminode 12, very short, glabrous; styles 3, hairy in lower half; stigmata pointed and divergent. Fruits sessile, ovoid, subdepressed, 1.5 by 2–2.5 cm (including cupule), on erect and infructescence 8–15 cm long. Cupule completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall sparsely covered with curved, woody, branched spines; dehiscent in 3–5 parts when dry. Nuts urceolate, triangular in outline, (1)–2–3 per cupule, glossy brown except the narrow apex, styles and stigmata persistent.

description: Tree, 6–40 m high, 70–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–10 by 3–4 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs greyish pubescent, glabrescent. Bark dark brown, rough, with longitudinal irregular fissures 2 cm thick; inner bark reddish; sapwood white. Leaves lanceolate or oblong, 7–21 by 3–6.5 cm; base obtuse, oblique; apex acuminate or acute, sometimes caudate; margins entire; coriaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, subdepressed on the upper, brownish on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface; lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, arched but not anastomosing; other veins indistinct. Petiole 1–1.8 cm, glabrous, black when dry. Inflorescences male and female mixed or separate, terminal or axillary, pubescent. description: Tree, 15–20 m high, 80–150 cm girth. Twigs glabrous, sparsely lenticellate, black when dry. Bark blackish, longitudinally furrowed. Leaves obovate or elliptic-oblong, 9–13.5 by 2.5–4.7 cm; base slightly cuneate; apex broadly acute to acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, dull to glossy on the upper surface, pale brown on the lower; midrib and nerves with sharp ridges on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins distinct on lower surface, reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1.2–2 cm, pubescent then glabrous, black when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal or axillary near shoot apex, 6–10 cm long, white hairy throughout. Male inflorescence branched, rarely simple; bracts and bracteoles narrowly triangular, 1–1.5 by 0.2 mm, glabrous outside, pubescent inside, ciliate. Male flowers in 3–5–7-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, ca 1 mm long, lobes divided ca halfway to the base, densely white hairy on both sides; stamens 12, 1.5–2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., densely white hairy. Female inflorescence usually below male. Female flowers always in 3–5-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent, pubescent in lower half; stigmata pointed. Acorns obconical, ca 1.5 by 1.2 cm (including cupule when young), fruit-stalk 2–5 mm on erect and woody infructescence 12–15 cm long; acorns free, indehiscent. Cupule obconical, completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall comprising grey to dark brown scales, arranged in 5–6 undulate rings or lamellae. Nut ovoid or conical, ca 1 by 0.7 cm.

description: Tree, 5–15 m high, 30–100 cm girth. Twigs densely tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark grey to dark grey, longitudinally furrowed; inner bark yellowish-brown to orange; sapwood yellowish. Leaves obovate, 13–28 by 5–14.5 cm; base slightly cuneate or obtuse, unequal; apex rounded, obtuse or shortly acute; margins entire; coriaceous, sparsely tomentose on the upper surface then glabrescent, except along midrib and nerves, densely tomentose on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 10–15 pairs, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper. Petiole 1–2 cm, tomentose. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate or few branched, axillary and terminal, tomentose. Male inflorescence spike 6–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, 2–2.5 by 0.5 mm, tomentose outside. Male flowers white to yellow, in 5–10-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, 1.5–2 mm long, ovate, divided ⅓ to ½ to the base, tomentose on both sides; stamens 12, 1–2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, hirsute. Female inflorescence spike, solitary or 2–3 in a tuft, 10–40 cm long. Female flowers in 3–10-flowered cluster; other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–5, divergent; stigmata pointed. Acorns sessile, conical, 2–2.5 by 1.2–1.5 cm (including cupule); on erect and unbranched infructescence, 16–40 cm long, the latter 0.5–1 cm in diam.; acorns connate near base (some free), indehiscent. Cupule cup-shaped, enclosing ½ or more of the nut; wall comprising alternate and greyish-brown scales, fused internally but the tips free and upward pointing. Nut 1, conical, 1.2–2 by 1–1.5 cm, indumentum dull greyish, glabrescent.

description: Tree, 10–15 m high, 60–90 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 1–2 by 1 mm, glabrous; bracts linear, with oily coating, glabrous. Twigs with 3–4 sharp, longitudinal ridges, then terete and glabrous. Bark brown to brownish-green with rough scales. Stipules linear lanceolate, ca 1 mm long, glabrous. Leaves lanceolate, lorate or linear, 14–20 by 2–2.5 cm; base slightly cuneate; apex acuminate to caudate; margins entire; chartaceous, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces, then glabrescent; midrib prominent on both surfaces; lateral nerves 14–20 pairs, faint on both surfaces, scalariform and reticulate veins inconspicuous. Petiole 2–3 mm long, glabrous, dark brown when dry. Inflorescences not seen. Acorns conical and subdepressed, 2–2.5 by 2.5–3.5 cm (including cupule); sessile or on fruit-stalk up to 2 mm long, on erect infructescences to 10 cm long, with sparsely grey indumentum. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing up to ⅕ of the nut; wall comprising grey-hairy scales, arranged in 5–7 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly ovoid or broadly conical, depressed both on top and more at base, 1.5–2 by 2.5–3 cm, with one persistent, strongly impressed horizontal ring in the middle of nut, apex conical; scar basal, flattened, 1.5–2 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 8–15 m high, 40–80 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid to ellipsoid, 4–5 by 1–2 mm; bracts ovate to linear. Twigs greenish-white, lenticellate, with 3–5 sharp ribs decurrent under leaf insertion. Bark greyish, shallowly fissured; inner bark pink to reddish-brown; sapwood white, heartwood dark brown. Stipules linear-acute to subulate, ca 5 by 2 mm. Leaves oblanceolate or lanceolate, 7–15 by 2.3–5 cm; base cuneate; apex acute, obtuse or acuminate; margins entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, pale or glaucous on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, conspicuous to hardly distinct on both surfaces. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, pubescent then glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, axillary and terminal, 9–20 cm long, pubescent. Male inflorescence spike; bracts and bracteoles ovate, 0.6–1 by 0.3–0.6 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white, scented, in 3–4-flowered cluster, rarely solitary; calyx 6-lobed, ca 2 mm long, lobes ovate divided by halfway to the base, pubescent on both sides; stamens 10–12, 2.5–3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike. Female flowers solitary or in (1)–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers, styles 3, conical, ca 1.2 mm long, then divergent; stigmata pointed. Acorns sessile, broadly ovoid, strongly depressed at both ends, apex conical, 2–2.5 by 3–4 cm (including cupule); on erect woody infructescence, 8–12 cm long acorns free, indehiscent. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing only the base of the nut; wall comprising greyish-brown scales, arranged in 5–7 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly conical, flattened at base, apex conical, 1.5–2.5 by 2–3 cm; scar basal, flattened to concave, 2–2.5 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 10–20 m high, 80–120 cm girth. Leaves oblong, obovate or elliptic-oblong, 11–19 by 4–9.5 cm; base obtuse or slightly cuneate, minutely oblique; apex caudate or acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous or coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, more or less glabrous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–11 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.8–1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, in panicles or spikes, terminal or axillary, 3–15 cm long, glabrous. Male inflorescence spicate or branched, spikelets 3–11 cm long; bracts and bracteoles, ca 2 by 1 mm, glabrous. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, united near base, ca 1 mm long; stamens 10–12, 3–4 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, 1–2 mm in diam., pilose. Female inflorescence spike 10–15 cm long. Female flowers solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, conical, 1–1.5 mm long, decurved; stigmata pointed, glabrous. Acorns ovoid or turbinate, 2–2.5 by 2.5–3 cm (including cupule); fruit-stalk 0.5–1.5 cm long, on erect and woody influctescence, 8–10 cm long; acorns free, hardly dehiscent. Cupule turbinate, base broader than the upper part, enclosing ca ⅘ of the nut; wall with densely greenish-yellow indumentum, with 5–6 conspicuous undulate horizontal filiform lines. Nut 1, ovoid, 1–1.5 by 2–2.5 cm greyish pubescent, especially around the umbo.

description: Tree, 7–15 m high, 100–150 cm girth. Terminal bud ovoid, glabrous, with oily coating, black when dry. Twigs glabrous. Leaves elliptic or elliptic-oblong, 8–18 by 3–5–10 cm; base obtuse, more or less oblique; apex caudate or acuminate; margins entire; chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface, pale on the lower, pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–11 pairs, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2.5 cm, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent, black when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate, rarely few branched, terminal and axillary, greyish pubescent. Male inflorescence spike 5–12 cm long; bracts and bractetoles, ovate acute, 2–3 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3–(5)-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, 1.5–2 mm long; lobes ovate, divided ca halfway to the base, pubescent outside. Female inflorescence spike 10–20 cm long; flowers solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Pedicel 2–3 mm long. Acorns ovoid or broadly turbinate, 1–1.8 by 1.5–2.3 cm (including cupule); fruit-stalk ca 1 cm long, on erect and woody infructescence 8–12 cm long; acorns free (those that develop), hardly dehiscent. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing base or up to ⅖ of the nut (when mature); wall comprising tomentose scales, arranged in 4–5 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly ovoid, 1–1.5 by 1.2–2 cm, depressed at both ends; scar basal.

description: Tree, 20–45 m high, 120–200 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–7 by 4–5 mm, tomentose; bracts ovate, acute. Twigs grey to blackish, glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, smooth or fissured; sapwood brownish. Stipules lanceolate, ca 5 by 2 mm, hairy on both sides. Leaves obovate, oblanceolate or elliptic, 10–30 by 4–14 cm; base cuneate or obtuse; apex broadly acute to acuminate; margins slightly serrate to entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glossy green on the upper surface, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, arched and more or less anastomosing, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 2–3 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, panicles or spikes, terminal or axillary, sometimes near the scars of fallen leaves, 2–2.4 cm long, pubescent. Male inflorescence spicate to few branched, spike or spikelets 10–24 cm long; bracts and bracteoles narrowly ovate acute, 1–1.2 by 0.5–1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers always in 3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, ca 1 mm long, lobes divided ca halfway to the base, pubescent on both sides; stamens 12, 3–4 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 0.5 mm in diam., hairy. Female inflorescence spike. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–5, conical, pubescent near base; stigmata pointed. Acorns (young) conical, 1–3.5 by 1–3.2 cm (including cupule); fruit stalk to 0.5 mm long, on an erect and woody infructescence, 6–13 cm long; acorns free, indehiscent. Cupule obconical, completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall comprising tomentose scales, arranged in 3–8 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly ovoid, 1–2.7 by 2–3.5 cm, depressed at both ends; scar to halfway up nut.

description: Tree, 10–25 m high, 60–150 cm girth. Twigs tomentose, glabrescent, sparsely lenticellate. Terminal buds ovoid, 2–4 by 1–2 mm; bracts ovate, acute. Stipules ovate, acute, 0.5–1 by 0.3–0.5 cm. Leaves oblong or ovate, 13–27 by 5–8.5 cm; base obtuse or broadly acute, oblique; apex acute to cuneate; margins entire, revolute; coriaceous, glabrous, dull to glossy green on the upper surface, densely tomentose then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 10–15 pairs, arched and more or less anastomsing, scalariform and reticulate veins fine, distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 3–5 cm. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, in panicles or spikes, terminal or axillary, 5–15 cm long, pubescent. Male inflorescence spicate or branched, spikelets 10–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles linear, acute, 1.5–3.5 by 0.5–1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers usually in 3–5-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, oblong, 1.5–2 mm long, lobes divided to halfway to the base, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, 1.5–2 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, 1–2 mm in diam., pilose. Female inflorescence spike 5–10 cm long. Female flowers solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, conical, 1–1.5 mm long, decurved; stigmata pointed, glabrous. Acorns jar-shaped or obconical, base much narrower than apex, 5–6 by 3–4 cm (including cupule); fruit-stalk ca 1 cm, on erect and woody infructescence 6–10 cm long; acorns free, hardly dehiscent. Cupule jar-shaped, base much narrow than apex, completely enclosing the nut and narrowly torose upward; wall smooth, with dense, greyish-brown indumentum and 3-4 distinct, horizontal filiform lamellae near apex only. Nut 1, obconical, 3.5–4 by 2.5–3.5 cm, flattened on top, with many longitudinal grooves.

description: Tree, 10–17 m high, 75–100 cm girth. Bark greyish-brown; inner bark dark brown. Leaves lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 9–17 by 2.5–6 cm; base obliquely obtuse; apex caudate or acuminate; margins entire; subcoriaceous, usually curved to one side, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, greenish to glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, slightly depressed on the upper, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 0.8–1 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate or paniculate, terminal and axillary, sparsely pubescent. Male inflorescence always a panicle, spikelets 5–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, 2–3 by 0.5–1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers greenish-white, scented, solitary or in 1–2–5-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, 1–1.5 mm long, lobes divided ⅓ to ½ to the base, pubescent on both surfaces; stamens 10–12, 3–3.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 8–24 cm long. Female flowers in (1)–3–5-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles (2)–3, pubescent near base, stigmata pointed. Acorns broadly ovoid, strongly depressed at both ends, 0.7–0.8 by 1–1.5 cm (including cupule), fruit-stalk 2–4 mm long, on erect and slender infructescence, 10–24 cm long; infructescence with many short branches, acorns fused or adnate near base (some free) but still distinct in shape, indehiscent. Cupule distinctly saucer-shaped, enclosing ¼ to ⅓ of the nut; wall comprising alternate greenish-brown scales, fused throughout, except the narrow, free apex. Nut 1, broadly ovoid, 0.5–0.6 by 1–1.2 cm; apex retuse or flattened; base flattened; dull brown.

description: Tree, 8–20 m high, 80–120 cm girth. Twigs tomentose, then glabrescent, lenticellate. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm; bracts ovate. Stipules linear, 8–10 by 2–3 mm. Leaves oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 11–19 by 3.5–5.5 cm; base slightly cuneate, obtuse; apex acuminate to caudate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous except midrib and nerves on both surfaces, young leaves with black oily coating; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 11–14 pairs, arched and more or less anastomosing, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–1.5, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate or rarely branched, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, 0.5–1 mm long; lobes ovate, divided ca ⅓ to the base, pubescent outside; stamens 12, ca 1 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 3–7 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers, styles 3–(4), divergent, stigmata pointed. Cupule ovoid, completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall comprising alternate scales, fused internally, except free, upward-pointing apex. Nut 1, ovoid to conical, 1– 1.5 by 0.8–1.2 cm.

description: Tree, 15–30 m high; 90–250 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm; bracts ovate, acute, pubescent outside. Twigs greyish tomentose then glabrous, dark greyish-brown, lenticellate. Stipules triangular, ca 1 by 0.5 mm. Bark greenish-brown to dark brown, rough; inner bark red. Leaves elliptic, ovate or elliptic-oblong, 10–18 by 5–8 cm; base obtuse, more or less symmetrical; apex minutely caudate, acute; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface, sparsely white hairs or glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; lateral nerves 10–14 pairs arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, in panicles or spikes, axillary or terminal, 7–20 cm long, pubescent. Male inflorescence simple or branched, spikes or spikelets 7–20 cm long; bracts and bracteoles linear-lanceolate, 1–2 by 0.2 mm, pubescent outside, ciliate. Male flowers yellowish, scented, solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, ca 1 mm long, lobes divided ¼ to ⅙ to the base, short hairy outside; stamens (10)–12, 3–3.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hairy. Cupule turbinate, base slightly narrower than the upper part, completely enclosing the nut except around the umbo; wall smooth, with short silky hairs then glabrescent, with 4–5 distinct, undulate, horizontal, filiform lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid, 1.5–1.7 by 1.8 cm, silky or white hairs then glabrescent.

description: Tree, 10–15 m high; 80–150 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark grey, rather smooth, lenticellate. Leaves oblong or elliptic-oblong, 12–15 by 6–7 cm, not whorled at end of twigs; base obtuse, slightly attenuate; apex acute; margins entire; coriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent on both surfaces; usually green on the upper surface, brownish on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–15 pairs, conspicuous on both surfaces, arched and more or less anastomosing, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–1.2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spikes or panicles, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male inflorescence a spike or branched, spikes or spikelets 7–14 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, 1–2 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, 1–1.5 mm long; lobes broadly triangular, divided ca ¼ to base, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike or 1–2-branched, spikes or spikelets 10–20 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, conical then divergent; stigmata pointed. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing ca ½ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, thin and triangular scales, fused throughout internally. Nut 1, ovoid, 0.5 by 1.3–1.4 cm, flattened at base, broadly convex on top with styles remnant.

description: Tree, 10–25 m high; 80–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid or ellipsoid, 4–5 by 2–3 mm; bracts linear, acute. Twigs glabrous. Bark greyish, longitudinally fissured. description: Tree, 5–20 m high, 45–100 cm girth. Twigs grey pubescent then glabrescent. Bark dark grey to brown, deeply furrowed, 2–3 cm thick; inner bark dark brown; sapwood brownish. Leaves oblong, ovate-lanceolate or elliptic, 9–23 by 3–8 cm; base obtuse, slightly cuneate; apex acute, acuminate to caudate; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, silver green to glaucous on the lower. Young leaves with black and sticky oily coating; midrib and nerves 8–10 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 0.5–2.2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spikes or panicles, terminal and axillary, pubescent. Male flowers yellowish white, scented, always solitary; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, up to 1 mm long, lobes ovate, divided ca ¼ to the base, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 2.5–3 mm long glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. description: Tree, 3–30 m high; 150–250 cm girth. Terminal bud ovoid to ellipsoid, 3–5 by 2–3 mm. Twigs sparsely pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate; inner bark yellowish-brown to brown; sapwood whitish. Stipules linear, 3–4 by 1 mm. Leaves narrowly elliptic, oblong, obovate to elliptic-oblong, 4–5 by 1–2 cm; base slightly cuneate, rarely obtuse; apex acute, acuminate to caudate; margins entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous and glossy green on the upper surface, sparsely pubescent and glaucous on the lower; midrib distinct on both surfaces; lateral nerves 10–13 pairs, more or less anastomosing; scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–3 mm long, glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal, 3–20 cm long, grey pubescent. Male inflorescence a panicle, spikelets 3–7–(20) cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 1 by 0.3 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers yellowish, scented, in 2–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, ca 1 mm long, divided by halfway to the base, pubescent outside; stamens 12, 2–3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 4–5 cm long. Female flowers solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–5, conical, 0.5–1 mm long; stigmata pointed. Acorns slightly obovoid to ovoid, 0.5–1.5 by 0.8–2 cm (including cupule); fruit-stalk 1–2 mm long, on erect and woody infructescence 4–5 cm long, acorns free, indehiscent. Cupule slightly obconical or saucer-shaped, enclosing ca ¼ of the nut; wall comprising scales with grey indumentum, arranged in 3–4 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, somewhat broadly ovoid, 1–1.3 by 1.5–1.8 cm, greenish-brown; scar basal, flattened, ca 1.2 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 5–30 m high; 40–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–10 by 2–3 mm; bracts lanceolate, pubescent on both sides. Leaves lanceolate or lanceolate-oblong, 9–26 by 3.5–8.5 cm; base slightly cuneate or obtuse; apex acuminate or caudate; margins entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, pubescent then glabrescent except along midrib and nerves on both surfaces; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 10–17 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–(2.5) cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate, terminal and axillary, grey pubescent. Male inflorescence a spike, rarely branched, spikes 10–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate-lanceolate, 3–8 by 0.2–0.3 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers yellowish, in 3–5-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, 0.5–1 mm long; lobes ovate, divided ca ½ to the base, pubescent on both sides; stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 0.5 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike, solitary, rarely 2–3 in a tuft, 10–20 cm long. Female flowers in 3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Acorns sessile, obconical, 2.5–4 by 2.5–3 cm (including cupule); on erect and slender infructescence, 10–12 cm long acorns free, dehiscent. Cupule obconical, completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall comprising alternate, pubescent, decurved pseudo-spines. Nut 1, ovoid to broadly conical, 1–1.5 by 1–1.5 cm; scar basal, up to ⅓ from base of the nut.

description: Tree, 10–30 m high; 90–120 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 mm; bracts ovate, acute, ca 2 by 1 mm. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, dark brown when dry lenticellate. description: Tree, 5–12 m high, 40–80 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 4–5 by 3–4 mm; bracts narrowly ovate to linear. Twigs densely tomentose, then glabrescent, sparsely lenticellate. Leaves obovate, 8.5–14 by 3–5 cm; base acute, more or less acute; apex obtuse to broadly acute, usually minutely emarginate; margins entire, strongly revolute; coriaceous, sparsely pubescent on both surfaces then glabrescent; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, flattened to depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 6–8 pairs, at first straight then arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole stout, 5–6 mm long, flattened adaxially. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate, rarely few branches, axillary and terminal, tomentose. Female inflorescence spike 5–10 cm long. Female flowers solitary or in 1–3-flowered cluster, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, more or less divergent, pubescent in lower half; stigmata pointed. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing ca ½ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, thin and triangular scales, fused in the lower half internally. Nut 1, ovoid, flattened at base, 2–2.5 by 3–4 cm, glabrous, glossy brown; scar basal, concave 2–2.5 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 15 m high; 50–100 cm girth. Twigs reddish-brown to greenish pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Leaves elliptic-oblong, 9–17 by 3–5 cm; base slightly cuneate; apex caudate-acuminate; margins entire; subcoriaceous to chartaceous, glabrous and dull green on the upper surface, pubescent and pale green then glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–12 pairs, arched but not anastomosing; long both midrib and nerves pinkish when dry, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 0.5–1 cm long pubescent then glabrescent, reddish to blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate or few branched, axillary and terminal, pubescent. Male flowers white to brownish-white, always in 3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, 1–1.5 mm long; lobes ovate, divided to halfway to the base, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, ca 0.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Cupule slightly obconical, enclosing ca ⅔ of the nut; wall comprising alternate and tomentose scales, fused internally, apex free, incurved. Nut 1, conical, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 cm, glossy brown, hairy on the umbo, scar basal, ca 1.2 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 5–20 m high; 40–120 cm girth. Terminal buds ellipsoid, 5–8 by 2–3 mm; bracts linear to lanceolate, tomentose. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. description: Tree, 15–40 m high, 100–180 cm girth. Twigs sparsely greyish pubescent then glabrous, spider-shaped lenticels. Leaves lanceolate or lanceolate oblong, 8–20 by 2–6.5 cm; base obliquely cuneate or obtuse; apex acuminate; margins entire; coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, pale green on the lower, usually curved to one side; midrib prominent on the lower surface, flattened or depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–13 pairs, conspicuous on the lower surface, hardly distinct on the upper, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Petiole 0.4–1.3 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal and axillary, pubescent.
