description: Tree, 5–20 m high; 30–145 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate, blackish when dry. Bark dark brown, scales thick, flaky; inner bark dark red; sapwood whitish, heartwood reddish-brown. Leaves ovate, ovate-oblong to obovate, 9–20 by 4–11 cm; base obtuse or slightly cuneate; apex caudate or acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface, glaucous on the lower; young leaves with black oily coating; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2 cm, pubescent then glabrous. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal and axillary, green or greyish pubescent. Female inflorescence spike 10–20 cm long, rarely branched. Female flowers solitary, rarely in clusters, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, conical, stigmata pointed. Acorns conical to slightly obconical 1.7–2 by 1.5–1.7 (including cupule); fruit-stalk ca 1 cm long, on erect and woody infructescence, 10–25 cm long; acorns free, indehiscent. Cupule slightly obconical, enclosing up to ½ of the nut; wall comprising alternate and thin scales, fused in the lower half, the upper free, more or less incurved at apex. Nut 1, conical to ovoid, 1.5–1.7 by 1.2–1.5 cm.

description: Tree, 6–30 m high; 40–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid to ellipsoid, 5–7 by 2–3 mm; bracts narrowly ovate, greyish pubescent outside. description: Tree, 5–25 m high, 60–150 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrous, sparsely lenticellate. Bark greyish to blackish, rather smooth ca 2 cm thick; inner bark reddish-brown. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal and axillary, tomentose. description: Tree, 5–15 m high, 50–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 1–1.5 by 0.7–1 cm; bracts ferruginous. Twigs greyish pubescent then glabrescent. Bark greyish-brown; inner bark pinkish-brown. Petiole 1.5–2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent, dark red to black when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spicate, rarely branched, in upper leaf scars, axillary and terminal, pubescent. description: Tree, 6–20 m high, 30–150 cm girth. Twigs greyish pubescent then glabrous. Bark brown to greyish-brown, fissured; inner bark reddish brown; sapwood white. description: Tree, 10–20 m high, 100–160 cm girth. Terminal buds obovoid, 1–2 by 1–1.5 cm, bracts lanceolate, with silvery hairs. description: Tree, 15–30 m high, 65–180 cm girth. Twigs grey, smooth, sparsely lenticellate. Bark greenish to greyish, smooth, lenticellate; inner bark reddish-brown with white stripes. Leaves oblong or elliptic-oblong, 10–21 by 3.5–7 cm; base obtuse or somewhat cuneate, strongly oblique; apex acute or acuminate; margins entire; chartaceous to subcoriaceous, greyish pubescent then glabrescent, glossy green on the upper surface, pale on the lower, unequal and usually curved to one side; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 14–20 pairs, arched and anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Male flowers greenish-white, smelling disagreeable, simple or in 1–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, campanulate, 1–1.5 mm long; lobes divided ca halfway to the base, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens (10)–12, ca 3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 8–18 cm long, rarely branched. Female flowers in (1)–3 flowered cluster, rarely solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–(4), conical then divergent; stigmata pointed; acorns sessile, broadly ovoid, 1–1.2 by 1.2–1.4 cm (including cupule), strongly depressed at both ends; on erect and slender infructescence, 7–20 cm long; developed acorns free or adnate 2–3, but not fused; indehiscent. Cupule cup-shaped or slightly conical, enclosing ⅕ to ½ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, thin, triangular scales, fused internally. Nut 1, flattened at both ends, 1–1.3 by 1.3–1.5 cm, sparsely covered with silver hairs, then glabrescent; scar flattened, ca 1.3 cm in diam., at base of nut only.

description: Tree, 6–25 m high, 40–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid to globose, 2–5 by 2–3 mm; bracts ovate to linear. Twigs greenish tomentose then glabrescent, sparsely lenticellate. Stipules lanceolate 2.5–5 by 1–1.5 mm. Leaves oblong or lanceolate-oblong, usually curved to one side, 11–25 by 3–6 cm; base obtuse or somewhat cuneate, oblique; apex acuminate, cuspidate, rarely acute; margins entire; subcoriaceous to chartaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrous, except on the lower surface; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 13–17 pairs, arched and anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 0.5–1 cm, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent, dark brown when dry. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal and axillary, greenish pubescent. Male inflorescence paniculate or spicate, spikes or spikelets 3–15 cm long; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white or greenish, in 3-flowered cluster, rarely solitary; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, ca.1 mm long; lobes ovate, divided ca halfway to the base, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 12, 2–2.5 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spikes 5–26 cm long, rarely branched. Female flowers in 2–5-flowered cluster, rarely solitary, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–(4) divergent, 1–3 mm long; stigmata pointed; acorns sessile, ovoid or obovoid, 1.5–2 by 1.1–1.5 cm (including cupule); on erect and slender infructescence, 5–20 cm long; acorns usually in clusters but not connate, indehiscent. Cupule slightly obconical or cup-shaped, enclosing up to ⅕ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, thin, triangular scales, fused in the lower half, free at apex. Nut 1, ovoid to conical, 1.5–1.7 by 1–1.5 cm, indumentum grey then dull brown.

description: Tree, 10–25 m high, 60–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 5–7 by 2–5 mm, bracts narrowly lanceolate. Twigs pubescent then glabrous, lenticellate. Bark brownish to greyish black, smooth or scaly, 1–2 cm thick; inner bark brownish-yellow with dark brown stripes; sapwood brownish or yellowish, heartwood dark brown. Leaves oblong, oblong-lanceolate, to lanceolate, 8–25 by 3–6.5 cm; base slightly cuneate or obtuse, oblique; apex acuminate to caudate; margins entire; chartaceous to subcoriaceous, softly pubescent on both surfaces then glabrescent, except along midrib and nerves especially on the lower surface; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–15 pairs, arched and more or less anastomosing, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface. Petiole stout, 0.5–1 cm, dark hairy. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, terminal and axillary, densely greenish pubescent. Male inflorescence spicate or few branched, spikes or spikelets resembling catkins, 4–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles narrowly triangular, 3–4 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white to yellowish, scented, usually in (1) 3–5-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, ca 1 mm long, lobes divided ⅓ to ½ to the base, pubescent outside, ciliate; stamens 10–12, 2–3 mm long, glabrous; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence catkin 5–20 cm long. Female flowers solitary and usually adnate but not fused together, other characters as in male flowers, styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Acorns sessile, broadly ovoid, 1.5–2 by 2–3 cm (including cupule), depressed at both ends, on erect and woody infructescence, 10–18 cm long; acorns adnate but not fused together, indehiscent. Cupule broadly cup-shaped, completely enclosing the nut except the umbo; wall comprising alternate pseudo-spines and free scales, pseudo-spines incurved or erect. Nut 1, broadly conical, up to 1.5 by 2 cm, sparsely sericeous then dull brown; scar basal, concave, ca 1.5 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 20–30 m high, 150–200 cm girth. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish; inner bark reddish-brown. Leaves oblong or elliptic-oblong, 10–26 by 4.5–9.5 cm, usually whorled at ends of twigs; base obtuse, slightly cuneate, asymmetric; apex acuminate or caudate, rarely acute; margins entire; coriaceous to subcoriaceous, pubescent then glabrescent on both surfaces; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–14 pairs, straight then curved near margins, not anastomosing, scalariform veins inconspicuous. Petiole 2–4 cm, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent. Inflorescences male and female separate or female below, spikes. Male inflorescence spike 5–10 cm long; bracts and bracteoles narrowly triangular, 2–3 by 1 mm, pubescent outside. Male flowers white to yellowish, usually in (1)–3-flowered cluster; calyx 6-lobed, broadly campanulate, ca 1 mm long, lobes divided ca halfway to the base, pubescent outside; stamens 10–12, 2–3 mm long; rudimentary ovary subglobose, ca 1 mm in diam., hirsute. Female inflorescence spike 5–10 cm long, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata pointed. Acorns sessile, broadly conical, 1–3 by 1.4–3 cm (including cupule); on erect and slender infructescence, 8–15 cm long, strongly depressed at both ends; acorns in clusters, more or less adnate but not fused (the develop one), well-spaced, indehiscent. Cupule cup-shaped, enclosing ca ½ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, thin, triangular scales, fused in the lower half internally, the apices free, pointing upward or reflexed. Nut 1, broadly ovoid or conical, apex convex, flattened at base, 0.8–1 by 1.2–2 cm, dull brown.

description: Tree, 10–25 m high, 50–150 cm girth. Buds and axillary ovoid, 0.6–1 by 0.3 mm, sparsely silky hairs outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate, usually with hairy galls along twig. Bark dark brown, longitudinally furrowed, 1–5 cm thick. Leaves oblong to oblong lanceolate, 7–19 by 3–9 cm; base obliquely obtuse or cordate; apex acuminate or caudate; margins strongly serrate with curved or straight, spine-like tips; chartaceous, pubescent then glabrescent, dull olive-green on the upper surface; yellowish on the lower; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 14–17 pairs, straight and protruding to end of serrate margins, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–7 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence a solitary catkin, pendulous, 6–8 cm long, tomentose. Male flowers solitary or in 3–4-flowered cluster. Female flowers free, 1 3 together; styles 3, connate near base; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, ovoid in outline, 2.5–3 by 3–5 cm (including cupule), always 1(2) acorns in each infructescence. Cupule coroniform, enclosing ⅕ to ½ of the nut; wall comprising two kind of scales, the lower triangular, adnate the upper elongate up to 1 by 0.3 cm, horizontal or decurved, inner side fused with nut. Nut ovoid or tubuliform, 2–2.5 by 1.5–1.7 cm, conic or truncate apex; scar up to ⅕ from the base of nut.

description: Tree, 10–35 m high, 120–200 cm girth. Twigs glabrous, inconspicuously lenticellate. Leaves elliptic, elliptic-oblong or oblong-lanceolate, 6–15 by 2–5 cm, not whorled at ends of twigs; base obtuse or slightly oblique; apex acuminate or cuspidate; margins serrate in apical third or entire; subcoriaceous to chartaceous, glabrous, glossy green on the upper surface; pale on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 8–11, conspicuous on the lower surface, scalariform and reticulate veins hardly distinct. Petiole 1–2 cm, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent, blackish when dry. Male inflorescence a simple, tufted, pendulous catkin, terminal or axillary, sometimes in upper leaf scars, 3–10 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, 3–5 by 1–2 mm, pubescent outside. Acorns sessile, ovoid, 2–2.1 by 1.7–1.9 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody influctescence 3–6 cm long, usually with 3–5 acorns in each infructescence. Cupule cup or dish-shap, enclosing to ½ or ⅔ of the nut, rim not dilated; wall comprising tawny pubescent scales, set in 7–8 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid or conical, 2 by 1.3–1.5 cm, pubescent then glossy brown except near the umbo; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 8–30 m high, 60–150 cm girth. Terminal buds with fringed bracts, 5–6 mm long, pubescent on both sides. Twigs densely tomentose, glabrescent. Bark greenish-brown, lenticellate; inner bark with sparse, needle-like ridges. Stipules linear, 4–8 mm long, tomentose outside. Leaves ± obovate, 9–18 by 3–6 cm, not whorled at ends of twigs; base ± cuneate or obtuse to suboblique; apex acute or obtuse; margins serrate in apical third, sometimes entire; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous except along midrib on both surfaces, dark to glossy green on the upper surface; pale to glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; lateral nerves 7–9 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–3.5 cm, pubescent, glabrescent, not black when dry. Male inflorescence not seen. Female inflorescence spike erect, terminal or axillary, 1–3 cm long, tomentose, each spike 1–4-flowered, free. Perianth 6-lobed, tomentose; styles 3–6, hirsute in lower half, 3 mm long, divergent; stigmata elongate, black. Acorns sessile, ovoid, 3–3.5 by 2.2 cm (including cupule) on short infructescence, usually with 1–2 acorns in each infructescence. Cupule cup or dish-shaped, enclosing to ⅔ of the nut, rim not dilated; wall comprising rusty brown scales, set in 7–8 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid, 2.5–3 by 2 cm, densely short hairs, scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 10–30 m high, 80–150 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, 1–1.5 by 0.8–1 cm; bracts ovate, tomentose outside. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent. Bark greenish, 1 cm thick, lenticellate; inner bark brown, brittle; cambium purplish-brown. Stipules linear-lanceolate, tomentose. Leaves oblong or slightly oblanceolate, usually curved to one side, 10–30 by 3–8.5 cm; base obtuse or slightly cuneate, oblique; apex acuminate or acute; margins serrate in upper half; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent, glossy green on both surfaces; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 14–18 pairs, arched and more or less anastomosing, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–1.5 cm, adaxial flat, pubescent then glabrescent. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary, 1–2 cm long, tomentose. Female flowers simple, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, connate; stigmata elongate. Acorns globose, flattened at base and apex, 1–1.5 by 1.5–1.7 cm (including cupule), fruit-stalk 1–1.2 cm, erect, usually one acorn in each infructescence. Cupule cup-shaped, reaching to apex of the nut, not enclosing the apex, rim not dilated; wall comprising pubescent scales, set in 6–9 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, ovoid, depressed at base and apex, ca 0.7 by 1–1.5 cm, with brown indumentum, then glabrous.

description: Tree, 3–20 m high, 40–160 cm girth. Twigs tawny pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark dark grey, greyish-brown, roughly cracked; sapwood whitish. Leaves obovate, elliptic, ovate to ovate-oblong, 8–19 by 4–10 cm; base slightly cuneate or obtuse; apex acute or obtuse; margins serrate, sometimes crenulate; coriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrous except along midrib and nerves on both surfaces; midrib and lateral nerves strongly prominent on the lower surface; subdepressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–12 pairs, straight then curved near margins, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface; more or less depressed on the upper. Petiole 1–3 cm, grey pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence simple pendulous catkins, in axils of upper leaf-scars on young twigs, 5–15 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles scabrous outside. Male flowers in 3–4-flowered cluster; perianth broadly campanulate, 6-lobed, ca 2 mm long, lobes obovate, 1–1.5 mm, divided to or nearly to the base, pubescent near base outside, ciliate; stamens 6, 2–3 mm long, hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary and in axils of upper leaf-scars, 3–5 cm long, grey pubescent, each spike more than ten-flowered, free, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3–4, connate; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, obconical, ovoid, 1–3 by 1–2.2 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence, 2–8 cm long, acorns free, many on each infructescence. Cupule obconical, enclosing ⅓–½ of the nut (enclosed completely except umbo, when young) rim not dilated; wall comprising grey hairy scales, set in 5–7 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, conical, 1–2 by 2–2.5 cm, greyish pubescent then glabrescent.

description: Tree, 8–20 m high, 60–100 cm girth. Twigs densely tomentose. Bark dark brown; sapwood yellowish. Stipules linear-lanceolate, 5–8 by 1 mm, with red woolly hairs outside, ciliate. Leaves obovate, obovate-oblong or oblong, 7–23 by 2.2–6 cm, always whorled at ends of twigs; base obtuse or slightly cuneate; apex broadly acute, acute or obtuse; margins usually serrate in apical third to half; coriaceous, glabrous, except sparse pubescence along midrib and nerves on the upper surface, pale on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; lateral nerves 8–11 pairs, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1.5–2.5 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence simple, tufted, pendulous catkins, axillary and terminal, 3–5 cm long, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles lanceolate, ca 2 by 1 mm, tomentose outside. Female inflorescence spike erect, terminal and axillary, 1–3 cm long, tomentose, each spike 3–5-flowered, free, other characters as in male flowers; styles 3, divergent; stigmata capitate. Cupule cup or dish-shaped, enclosing ⅓ to ½ of the nut, rim dilated when mature; wall comprising ferruginous tomentose scales, set in 9–12 rings or lamellae. Nuts ovoid, conical or tubular conical 3–4.5 by 1.5–1.7 cm; scar basal, ca 1 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 8–20 m high, 60–200 cm girth. Twigs ribbed, pale tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish-black, dull brown. Stipules lanceolate, ca 1 cm long, pilose, not early caducous. Leaves ovate, elliptic, oblong or slightly tetrangular, 3.5–11 by 1.5–6 cm; base cordate or obtuse; apex acute; margins serrate, setaceous at ends of teeth; coriaceous or subcoriaceous, glabrous on the upper surface; pubescent then glabrescent on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; usually depressed on the upper, hairy along nerves; lateral nerves 6–9 pairs, straight, terminating beyond the serrate margins, scalariform veins hardly distinct. Male flowers solitary or in 1–3 flowered cluster; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, pilose outside. Perianth 4–7 lobed, lobes narrowly triangular, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, pilose outside; stamens 5–10, 1–2 mm long, hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect or reflexed, terminal or axillary, ca 1 cm long. Female flowers free; styles 3, connate; stigmata capitate. Acorns globose, ca.1 cm in diam. (including cupule), fruit stalk 2–3 mm long on erect infructescence up to 1 cm long, each infructescence with (1)–2 acorns. Cupule cup or saucer-shaped (globose when young), enclosing ⅓ to ½ of the nut (enclosed completely, when young); wall comprising alternate, thin, pubescent scales. Nut 1, ovoid-globose, to 1 cm in diam., depressed at apex.

description: Tree, 6–25 m high, 60–230 cm girth. Twigs densely tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark blackish, deeply longitudinally furrowed, 3–4 cm thick; inner bark reddish to dark brown. Leaves oblong or elliptic-oblong, 10–26 by 5–12 cm; base obtuse, usually oblique; apex acute or acuminate; margins serrate in the upper half; coriaceous but brittle, pubescent then glabrescent on the upper surface, except along midrib, densely velutinous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 12–16 pairs, straight and running into the teeth of margins, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface; depressed on the upper. Petiole 1.5–3 cm, densely tomentose. Male inflorescence a simple, pendulous catkin, 10–15 cm long, in the upper leaf-scars of young twigs, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles linear, ca 3.5 mm long, pilose outside, ciliate. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing to ⅕ of the nut or supporting base only; wall comprising greyish-brown hairy scales, set in 7–10 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, apex flat to minutely retuse, ca 1–1.5 by 2–3 cm, glaucous or with grey pubescent; scar basal, only, 2–3 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 5–40 m high, 50–150 cm girth. Terminal bud ovoid, 4–5 by 3 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs pubescent then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark blackish-brown, deeply furrowed, 2–3 cm thick; inner bark yellowish-brown; sapwood whitish, heartwood brown. Stipules linear, ca 5 mm long, pubescent. Leaves oblong, ovate-oblong or lanceolate; 10–24 by 3–10 cm; base obtuse; apex acute; margins serrate; subcoriaceous, densely pubescent, especially on the lower surface, then glabrescent except along midrib and nerves on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 15–17 pairs, straight to tips of serrate margins, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence 2–5 pendulous, simple or few branched, tufted catkins, 3–10 cm long in upper leaf-scars or axillary on young twigs, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles ovate, acute, ca 3 by 1 mm, tomentose outside, ciliate. Cupule obconical, completely enclosing nut; wall comprising grey to brown hairs and scales, set in 5–10 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, flat to minutely retuse at apex, ca 1 by 1.5–2 cm, indumentum brown, then glabrescent.

description: Tree, 7–30 m high, 60–200 cm girth. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark dark brown with greyish patches, irregularly fissured, ca 1 cm thick; inner bark dark yellow, pinkish or reddish-brown, scented. Stipules linear-lanceolate, ca 1 by 0.2 mm, pilose. Leaves oblong, elliptic, ovate or obovate, 8–20 by 3.5–8 cm; base obtuse or cuneate, more or less oblique; apex acute, rarely obtuse; margins serrate; subcoriaceous, pubescent then glabrescent on the upper surface, densely to sparsely tomentose except along nerves on the lower, dark green on the upper surface; midrib and lateral nerves prominent on the lower; depressed on the upper surface; lateral nerves 9–14 pairs, rather straight to tips of serrate margins, scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2–(4), pubescent, glabrescent. Male inflorescence solitary or tufted pendulous catkins, axillary near ends of twigs, 10–15 cm long, tomentose. Perianth (5–)6-lobed, lobes narrowly triangular, 1–1.5 by 0.5 mm, tomentose outside, ciliate; stamens 6–8, 2.5–3 mm long, hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect, 1–3 cm long. Female flowers free, 3–10 together; styles 3, connate; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, obconical, 1.4–2.5 by 1.4–3.5 cm (including cupule); on erect and woody infructescence 1–4 cm long. Cupule obconical, enclosing ¾ to ⅚ of the nut; wall comprising alternate scales with thick, incurved apices. Nuts ovoid or ellipsoid, depressed at base and apex, 1.7–2.5 by 1.5 cm, dark brown, silky pubescent around the umbo.

description: Tree, to 10 m high. Leaves lanceolate or lanceolate-oblong, rarely elliptic or ovate, 9–30 by 3.5–11 cm; base obtuse; apex acute to acuminate; margins serrate in apical one third to half; subcoriaceous to coriaceous, sparsely pubescent then glabrescent on the upper surface; densely pubescent, usually glaucous on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; subdepressed to strongly depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 15–27 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, scalariform veins conspicuous on the lower surface; usually depressed on the upper. Petiole 1.5–3 cm, sparsely pubescent. Male inflorescence not seen. Female inflorescence spike axillary, erect, 1–3 cm long, densely tomentose. Female flowers free, 2–10 in each spike; styles 4, densely tomentose in lower half; stigmata capitate. description: Tree, 6–20 m high, 40–80 cm girth. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, irregularly cracked. Stipules obovate, scarious, pilose outside, caducous. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm, tomentose, blackish when dry. (including cupule), on erect infructescence 2–4 cm long, each infructescence with 4–7-acorns. description: Tree, 10–40 m high, 80–250 cm girth. Buds ovoid or rounded; bracts ovate, 3–4 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. description: Tree, 10–35 m high, 100–200 cm girth. Terminal buds globose, ovoid, pubescent then glabrescent. Twigs densely pubescent then glabrous, dark grey, lenticellate. description: Tree, 9–30 m high, 40–180 cm girth. Axillary buds globose, ca 2 mm in diam., glabrous. Twigs lenticellate, blackish when dry. Bark dark grey, ca 2 cm thick, scaly; inner bark reddish; sapwood 25–30 cm thick, white. Petiole 1–3 cm, glabrous. description: Tree, 8–30 m high, 70–150 cm girth. Buds ovoid, slightly 4-angular, ca 4 by 3 mm; bracts ovate, acute, ca 10 by 1 mm, ciliate. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, blackish when dry. description: Tree, 18–25 m high, 120–200 cm girth. Buds rounded, ca 2 mm in diam., tomentose. Twigs pubescent then glabrous, lenticellate, blackish when dry. Stipules lanceolate, ca 10 by 2 mm, sparsely hairy near base, ciliate. description: Tree, 7–20 m high, 60–100 cm girth. Terminal buds ovoid, ca 3 by 2 mm, pubescent then glabrescent. description: Tree, 4–25 m high, 60–160 cm girth. Twigs reddish-brown hairy, then glabrescent. Bark greyish; inner bark reddish-brown or brown, 1–4 cm thick. description: Tree, 15–35 m high, 100–300 cm girth, usually with buttresses to 5 m high. Budsovoid, ca 5 by 3 mm; bracts ovate, acute, hairy outside. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. description: Tree, to 12 m high. Budsovoid, ca 2 by 1.5 mm, glabrous. Twigs glabrous, blackish when dry. description: Tree, 10–25 m high, 80–100 cm girth. Budsovoid, ca 2 by 1 mm., covered with thin ovate scales, glabrous. Twigs densely tomentose, then glabrous, drooping. Bark blackish-brown, scales defoliating in patches. Stipules linear, 5–7 by 1 mm, sparsely glandular hairs. Leaves oblong, lanceolate-oblong, ovate or obtetragonal, 3.5–10 by 1.5–4 cm; base obliquely cuneate, obtuse or cordate; apex acute, acuminate to cuspidate; margins serrate or setaceous at apical half; subcoriaceous, coppery or reddish-brown when dry, pubescent along midrib and nerves on the lower surface, glossy green on the upper, domatia present; midrib prominent on the lower surface, depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 9–15 pairs, conspicuous on the lower surface, subdepressed on the upper or hardly distinct on either surface. Petiole 4–8 mm long, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence not seen. Female inflorescence spike, erect, 3–7 cm long, pubescent, glabrescent. Male flowers free, in 3–10-flowered cluster, styles 3, connate; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, obconical then conical in maturity, 1–1.5 by 0.7–1 cm (including cupule), on erect and woody infructescence 5–10 cm long. Cupule obconical (sometimes cup-shaped at maturity), enclosing ¼ to ⅔ of the nut; wall comprising alternate, evenly thin, hairy scales. Nut ovoid, ca 1.5 by 0.8 cm, conical at apex; scar basal, ca 0.8 cm in diam.

description: Tree, 10–30 m high, 80–150 cm girth. Terminal buds globose or slightly obovoid; bracts ovate, tomentose outside, ciliate. Twigs tomentose then glabrescent, lenticellate. Bark greyish-brown, reticulately fissured, 2–2.5 cm thick; inner bark purplish. Leaves oblong, elliptic oblong or obovate-oblong, 10–24 by 3.5–9 cm; base obliquely, obtuse to cuneate; apex acute or acuminate; margins minutely serrate in apical one third; coriaceous, hairy on both surfaces, more densely on the lower; midrib and nerves prominent on the lower surface; depressed on the upper; lateral nerves 12–20 pairs, curved near margins, scalariform veins fine, distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 1–2.3 cm, pubescent then glabrescent. Male inflorescence a catkin, simple, or 2–3 in a tuft, pendulous, 5–13 cm long, axillary or terminal, tomentose; bracts and bracteoles narrowly lanceolate, ca 3 by 0.5 mm, tomentose outside, ciliate. Male flowers in 2–5-flowered cluster; perianth broadly campanulate, (5)–6-lobed, 1–1.5 mm long, lobes obovate, divided halfway to base or nearly free, pubescent outside; stamens 10–12), ca 2 mm long, anthers hairy, filaments hairy near base. Female inflorescence spike erect, axillary, 5–10 cm long, tomentose, each spike with many free flowers; other characters as in male flowers; styles 5–6, divergent, tomentose; stigmata capitate. Acorns sessile, ovoid to slightly obovoid, 2–2.5 by 3–3.5 cm (including cupule), strongly depressed at both ends, on woody infructescence, acorns free. Cupule saucer-shaped, enclosing ½ to ¾ of the nut, rim dilated; wall comprising tomentose scales, the truncate apex of scales fused with the wall, set in 6–8 rings or lamellae. Nut 1, broadly ovoid, 1.5–2 by 2.5–3 cm, strongly depressed at both ends, apex slightly convex.

description: Tree, 15–30 m high, 100–200 cm girth. Bark brown to dark brown; outer part scaly, inner part with fine long and narrowed ridge, always depressed; sapwood as narrow canals. Interpetiolar stipules narrowly triangular, ca 3 by 1 mm. Leaves elliptic to more or less obovate, 6–12 by 2–5.5 cm; base cuneate; apex acute; subcoriaceous, green and shiny on the upper surface; pale on the lower; midrib prominent on the lower surface, lateral nerves 10–15 pairs, finely ridged on the lower; scalariform veins distinct on the lower surface. Petiole 0.5–1.5 cm long, glabrous, flat at adaxial, petiole and midrib pinkish when dry. Male inflorescences suberect, 3–10 cm long, puberulous throughout. Male flowers sessile, perianth campanulate, 6 lobed, free or minutely connate near base; stamens 6; anthers ovoid, basifixed; rudimentary ovary a cluster of hairs. Female inflorescences catkin erect, perianth as male, adnate to ovary at base; staminodes 6; styles 3, decurved or connate near base; stigmata capitate. Cupule sessile, broadly saucer-shaped, ca 1 cm in diam., with 7 or more irregular lobes, all covered with brown hairs, glabrescent, normally bearing 1–3 nuts. Nut prominently longitudinally triangular ridged, 5–10 by 6 mm (young), densely, brown hairs then glabrous and shiny.
